welcome.name: Welcome
welcome.content:
Welcome to the 'discord-player-music' page!



## About **Discord Player Music is a powerful [Node.js](https://nodejs.org) music module for your [discord.js](https://discord.js.org) bot. It is based on Promises, fully typed and has a lot of features.** * 👍 Simple & easy to use * 😄 Beginner friendly * 🎶 Replaceable track sources: YouTube through `youtubei.js` with an automatic `yt-dlp` fallback * 📃 YouTube playlist links * 🎸 Audio filters * 📝 Lyrics * 📂 Multiple servers * 🧩 Typed errors, JSDoc for the whole API, ESM and CommonJS ## Installation **Node.js 22.12.0 or newer and discord.js 14.28 or newer are required.** ```sh-session $ npm install discord-player-music discord.js $ yarn add discord-player-music discord.js $ pnpm add discord-player-music discord.js ``` Audio is converted with FFmpeg, which comes with the `ffmpeg-static` package. Some package managers do not run install scripts by default (npm 12 and pnpm 10 ask you to allow them): if the FFmpeg binary is missing, allow the install script of `ffmpeg-static` (`npm install-scripts approve ffmpeg-static`) or install FFmpeg in your system, the module finds it in `PATH`. [yt-dlp](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp) is used as a fallback source for YouTube. **You do not need to install it:** if it is not found in `PATH`, the module downloads the official binary from GitHub into `~/.cache/discord-player-music`, checks its checksum and updates it once a day. See the [Providers page](providers.md) to change or disable that. ## Example Usage ```js import { Client, GatewayIntentBits } from 'discord.js'; import { Player, PlayerError } from 'discord-player-music'; const client = new Client({ intents: [ GatewayIntentBits.Guilds, GatewayIntentBits.GuildMessages, GatewayIntentBits.GuildVoiceStates, GatewayIntentBits.MessageContent ] }); const player = new Player(client); player.on('ready', () => console.log('Player is ready!')); player.on('playingTrack', track => track.channel.text.send(`Now playing: **${track.title}**`)); player.on('error', ({ error }) => console.error(error)); client.on('messageCreate', async message => { if(!message.content.startsWith('!play ') || !message.member?.voice.channel) return; try { // A track title or a link to a video or a playlist const tracks = await player.search(message.content.slice(6), message.member, message.channel); // A link is added to the queue by itself, for a title the first result is taken if(tracks[0].searchType.includes('title')) await player.initQueueTrack(1, tracks); }catch(error) { message.channel.send(error instanceof PlayerError ? error.message : 'Something went wrong!'); } }); client.login('YOUR_CLIENT_TOKEN_HERE'); ``` More examples are in the [`examples`](https://github.com/xyligan-gp/discord-player-music/tree/stable/examples) folder. ## Good to know * **Methods throw errors.** Every method rejects with a `PlayerError` that has a `code` (for example `QUEUE_NOT_FOUND`), so use `try/catch` (or `.catch()`). * **YouTube changes often.** Any YouTube library can stop working after a change on YouTube's side. That is why the module has several sources: when `youtubei.js` is refused, `yt-dlp` plays the track and the module remembers it for the next tracks. See the [FAQ](faq.md) if a track does not play, and the [Providers page](providers.md) to change the order of the sources or write your own. * **Respect the rules.** Downloading streams is against the YouTube Terms of Service, and some hosting providers are blocked by YouTube. Use the module at your own risk. ## Links * NPM: [Open](https://www.npmjs.com/package/discord-player-music) * GitHub: [Open](https://github.com/xyligan-gp/discord-player-music) * Examples: [See](https://github.com/xyligan-gp/discord-player-music/tree/stable/examples) * Module Developer: [xyligan](https://github.com/xyligan-gp) * Developer Discord: [xyligan / @whatisgif](https://discord.com/users/533347075463577640) * Support Server: [Join xyligan development](https://discord.gg/zzbkvCcu2r)

♥ Thanks for using Discord Player Music ♥

faq.name: FAQ
faq.content:
# Frequently Asked Questions

These questions are some of the most frequently asked.

## What do I need to run the module?
* **Node.js 22.12.0 or newer** and **discord.js 14.28 or newer**.
* The bot needs the `Guilds`, `GuildVoiceStates` intents and, to read commands from messages, `GuildMessages` and `MessageContent`. It must have the *Connect* and *Speak* permissions in the voice channel.
* Everything else is installed with the module: `@discordjs/voice`, FFmpeg (`ffmpeg-static`) and an Opus encoder (`opusscript`). You do not need to install `@discordjs/opus`. If you want a faster native encoder, install `@discordjs/opus` yourself, the module will use it.

## There is no sound / FFmpeg was not found
The FFmpeg binary is downloaded by the install script of the `ffmpeg-static` package. Some package managers do not run install scripts by default (npm 12, pnpm 10). Allow the script (for example `npm install-scripts approve ffmpeg-static`, then `npm rebuild ffmpeg-static`) or install FFmpeg in your system: the module uses `ffmpeg` from `PATH` when the downloaded binary does not exist.

## A track does not play / I see `YouTube does not allow to download the whole audio (status 403)`
YouTube does not give the audio of some videos to the main source (`youtubei.js`) without a *PO token*, a proof that the request comes from a real client. In that case the module uses the next provider, **yt-dlp**, and you will see this line in the log of `providerFailed` events. After one such failure the module sends the next tracks (any videos) to yt-dlp first for 10 minutes, then tries the main source again. This is normal. The order of the sources and the other options are described on the [Providers page](providers.md).

If the track still does not play (the `error` event says that all providers failed):
1. Check that yt-dlp works: `new YtDlpProvider()` finds `yt-dlp` in `PATH` or downloads it, and needs access to GitHub. Without internet access to GitHub install it yourself (`pip install yt-dlp`, `winget install yt-dlp.yt-dlp`, a package of your system) or give the path with the `command` option.
2. Update yt-dlp: YouTube changes often and old versions stop working. The binary downloaded by the module is checked every time the player starts (at most once per hour): when a newer release exists, the module downloads it; an yt-dlp that you installed yourself you update yourself (`yt-dlp -U`).
3. The video can be unavailable in your country, private, age-restricted or removed. Age-restricted videos need cookies: `new Player(client, { cookies: 'cookies.txt' })` (see the question about cookies below).
4. If the bot runs on a hosting, its IP address can be blocked by YouTube ("Sign in to confirm you're not a bot"). Use cookies (see the question about cookies on a server below) or a proxy (`extraArgs: ['--proxy', 'http://host:port']`) or run the bot from another network. Using the cookies of your account can lead to its ban, use a separate account.

## An age-restricted video does not play (`SIGN_IN_REQUIRED`)
Videos with an age restriction can be played only by a signed-in account that is allowed to watch them, so both sources fail and `player.search()` rejects with `SIGN_IN_REQUIRED` (`error.cause` has the details). Give the cookies of such an account, see the next question: `new Player(client, { cookies: '/path/to/cookies.txt' })`.

## Do I need cookies on a Linux server (without a browser)?
**Often not**, so try without them first. YouTube asks to sign in ("Sign in to confirm you're not a bot") mostly when the IP address of the bot belongs to a hosting provider or a data center, and it depends on the provider and on the time. If it happens, the error of the track says it and mentions the `cookies` option. What you can do, from the most reliable:

1. **Cookies of an account.** yt-dlp can use the cookies of a signed-in YouTube account. A server has no browser, so export the cookies on a computer with a browser and copy the file to the server:
   * sign in to YouTube in a **private (incognito) window** with a **separate Google account** (not your main one: using cookies can get an account banned),
   * export the cookies of `youtube.com` in the Netscape format (for example with the browser extension *Get cookies.txt LOCALLY*, or on your computer `yt-dlp --cookies-from-browser chrome --cookies cookies.txt --skip-download "https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dQw4w9WgXcQ"`),
   * **close the private window** right away: YouTube rotates the cookies of an open browser session, and an exported copy becomes invalid,
   * put `cookies.txt` on the server (not into git!) and pass the path in the `cookies` option of the player: **one file is used by both sources**, `yt-dlp` (`--cookies`) and `youtubei.js` (signed-in session):

   ```js
   new Player(client, { cookies: '/path/to/cookies.txt' });

   // or for your own list of sources
   new Player(client, { sources: [new YoutubeiProvider({ cookies: '/path/to/cookies.txt' }), new YtDlpProvider({ cookies: '/path/to/cookies.txt' })] });
   ```

   The cookies expire after some time (weeks or months): when tracks stop playing again with the sign-in error, export them again.
2. **A proxy or another network.** If the IP address is blocked, use a proxy in the same way (`new YtDlpProvider({ extraArgs: ['--proxy', 'http://user:password@host:port'] })`) or run the bot from another network (for example from a home server). Residential proxies work better than data center ones.
3. **A PO token provider for yt-dlp.** There is a yt-dlp plugin that makes PO tokens on a server (`bgutil-ytdlp-pot-provider`, it works without a browser). It is an advanced option, see the yt-dlp documentation about PO tokens.

The module reads the file and uses the cookies of `youtube.com` only for requests to YouTube; it does not save or send them anywhere else. `youtubei.js` uses them for the information of age-restricted videos and for private playlists (its iOS client, which receives the audio, does not accept cookies), the audio of such videos is played by yt-dlp. If the file is missing or has no valid cookies (they expired), the provider reports it with the `error` event when the player starts. yt-dlp updates the cookies file by itself while it works (YouTube rotates some cookies), so give the process the right to write to it.

## How do I see which source plays a track?
Listen to these events (they are meant for debugging and for telling the users what happens):

```js
// Which source gives the audio of a track, and whether it was prepared in advance (the next track is prepared before the current one ends).
// `via` is set when a provider plays the audio of another one (for example a provider that finds the audio of a track in another source)
player.on('sourceUsed', ({ provider, via, track, seek, prefetched }) => console.log(`${provider}${via ? ` (${via})` : ''} plays ${track.title}`));

// Every step of finding, checking, downloading and updating yt-dlp (it starts when the player is created)
player.on('ytdlpStatus', ({ stage, message, version, latest }) => console.log(`[yt-dlp] ${stage}: ${message}`));

// A source failed and the module moves to the next one
player.on('providerFailed', ({ provider, method, error }) => console.warn(`${provider} failed to ${method}: ${error.message}`));

// No source could play the track: it is skipped and the queue goes on with the next one (`next` is null at the end of the queue)
player.on('skippedTrack', ({ track, next, error }) => console.warn(`Skipped ${track.title}: ${error.message}`));
```

The `error` event is emitted for the same failed track too, `skippedTrack` adds the next track and is easier to use for a message to the users.

Every track has a `source` field with the name of the provider that found it (`youtubei` or `yt-dlp`).

## Can I play a playlist?
Yes, give a link to a YouTube playlist (`https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=...` or a video link with `list=...`) to `player.search()`: all its tracks (up to `playlistLimit`, 100 by default) are added to the queue and playback starts from the first one. Automatic mixes (`list=RD...`), *Liked videos* and *Watch later* cannot be loaded.

## How do I make the bot play related tracks when the queue ends (autoplay)?
Turn the autoplay on: `new Player(client, { autoplay: true })` for all new queues, or `player.queue.setAutoplay(guildID, true)` for one queue (it switches the status when you do not pass it). When the tracks are over and no loop is on, the module finds related tracks, adds them and goes on playing, until the autoplay is turned off. **`autoAddingTracks` is not the autoplay:** it only adds the result of `player.search()` to the queue. Details: the [Providers page](providers.md#autoplay-and-related-tracks).

## Is there a pause between tracks?
The module prepares the next track in advance (20 seconds before the current one ends, see `prefetchSeconds`), so there should be none. The first track of a queue needs a moment to start (up to 5 seconds with yt-dlp).

## Why do I get `PlayerError` instead of an object with `error`?
Starting with version 2.0 methods throw errors instead of returning `{ error: { code, message } }`. See the [updating page](updating.md) for the full list of changes.

```js
try {
	await player.queue.skipTrack(message.guild.id);
}catch(error) {
	if(error instanceof PlayerError && error.code === PlayerErrorCode.QUEUE_NOT_FOUND) return message.channel.send('Nothing is playing!');

	throw error;
}
```

## Why does the bot sometimes just crash?
Always handle the errors of the methods (`try/catch`) and listen to the `error` event: an `error` event without listeners is only printed to the console, but an unhandled rejection of your own code can stop the process. Look at the error message and the `code` of `PlayerError`; if you can not solve it, contact the support server.

## Do the lyrics work for any language?
Lyrics are taken from the free [LRCLIB](https://lrclib.net) service, which has songs in many languages (for example Russian songs). Write the artist and the title in the query: `player.lyrics('Artist Title')`. You can use another service with your own `LyricsProvider` (the `lyrics` option).

## Is it allowed to use the module with YouTube?
Downloading streams is against the YouTube Terms of Service, and the authors of the module do not give legal advice. You use the module at your own risk. The module does not bypass authorization or DRM, it does what yt-dlp and similar tools do.

# Updating page

This documentation page is a short list of changes to your code that will have to be done when switching to a specific version of discord-player-music!

## 1.1.5
In version 1.1.5, `discord-player-music` was completely rewritten for the manager system.

### Player Constructor

```diff
+ options.searchResultsLimit
+ options.synchronLoop
+ options.defaultVolume

+ options.collectorsConfig.autoAddingSongs
+ options.collectorsConfig.maxAttempts
+ options.collectorsConfig.time
```

### Player Methods Update
#### CollectorsManager

```diff
+ player.collectors.message
```

#### VoiceManager

```diff
- player.joinVoiceChannel
+ player.voice.join

- player.leaveVoiceChannel
+ player.voice.leave
```

#### UtilsManager

```diff

+ player.utils.checkNode
+ player.utils.checkOptions
+ player.utils.checkPermissions
+ player.utils.createCollector
```

## 2.0.0
Version 2.0.0 fixes the playback of YouTube tracks: the old `ytdl-core` and `yt-search` libraries stopped working, so the source layer was rewritten. **All method and event names of 1.1.7 are kept**, but errors work in a different way and some requirements changed.

### Requirements

```diff
- Node.js 16.9.0
+ Node.js 22.12.0
- discord.js 14 (any)
+ discord.js 14.28

- @discordjs/voice 0.11
+ @discordjs/voice 0.19 (installed with the module)

- ytdl-core, yt-search
+ youtubei.js, yt-dlp (downloaded automatically)

- @discordjs/opus (required)
+ opusscript (installed with the module, @discordjs/opus is optional)
```

### Errors are thrown, not returned (breaking)

In 1.x many methods returned `{ error: { code, message } }`. Now every method **rejects with a `PlayerError`**. It has `code` (`PlayerErrorCode`), `status` (a number like HTTP: `404`, `400`, `409`, `502`...), `message` and `cause` (the original error, for example of a source provider).

```diff
- const skipData = await player.queue.skipTrack(guildID);
- if(skipData?.error) return message.channel.send({ content: skipData.error.message });
-
- message.channel.send({ content: `Skipped: ${skipData.current.title}` });
+ try {
+     const skipData = await player.queue.skipTrack(guildID);
+
+     message.channel.send({ content: `Skipped: ${skipData.current.title}` });
+ }catch(error) {
+     if(error instanceof PlayerError) return message.channel.send({ content: error.message });
+
+     throw error;
+ }
```

Error codes (`PlayerErrorCode`):

| Code | When |
| --- | --- |
| `MISSING_PARAMETER`, `INVALID_TYPE`, `INVALID_VALUE` | A parameter is missing or invalid (this was a thrown `PlayerError` in 1.x too) |
| `QUEUE_NOT_FOUND`, `QUEUE_TRACK_NOT_FOUND` | The server has no queue, or the queue has no track with that index |
| `SHUFFLE_UNAVAILABLE` | The queue has less than 3 tracks (the playing track is not shuffled) |
| `INVALID_STATE` | The queue is already in the requested state (paused or playing) |
| `FILTER_NOT_FOUND`, `FILTER_EXISTS` | Filters |
| `USER_NOT_IN_VOICE`, `ALREADY_CONNECTED`, `CONNECTION_FAILED`, `GUILD_NOT_FOUND` | Voice channels and servers |
| `TRACK_NOT_FOUND`, `LYRICS_NOT_FOUND` | Search and lyrics (`cause` has the reason, for example a source provider error) |
| `SIGN_IN_REQUIRED` | YouTube asks to sign in to play the video (age-restricted, or the server was taken for a bot): the cookies of an account are needed, see the FAQ |
| `COLLECTOR_NO_RESULTS`, `COLLECTOR_UNKNOWN`, `COLLECTOR_SMALL_VALUE`, `COLLECTOR_LARGE_VALUE`, `COLLECTOR_TIMEOUT`, `COLLECTOR_CANCELLED` | Collectors (`createCollector()` now rejects with `COLLECTOR_TIMEOUT` when nothing is selected in time, in 1.x it never finished; `COLLECTOR_CANCELLED` when the user cancels; the attempts used up by wrong answers end with `INVALID_VALUE`, `COLLECTOR_SMALL_VALUE` or `COLLECTOR_LARGE_VALUE`) |
| `SOURCES_FAILED` | Every source provider failed |
| `SOURCE_RATE_LIMITED`, `SOURCE_UNAUTHORIZED`, `AUDIO_NOT_FOUND` | A service limits the requests / did not accept the credentials / the audio of a track was not found in the other sources |

The type `ErrorData` and the `PlayerError` typedef with `{ channel, requested, method, error }` (it described the `error` event) were renamed to `PlayerErrorEvent`. The messages are the same as before (`player.errors` still exists).

The `error` event is emitted for errors that happen in the background (a track that can not be played, a lost voice connection) and now has the same data as before: `{ channel, requested, method, error }`. An `error` event without listeners is printed to the console and no longer crashes the process.

### Autoplay

New in 2.0.0: when the tracks are over, the module can find tracks related to the track that played last, add them to the queue and go on playing them, again and again, until the autoplay is turned off. It works only when neither the track loop nor the queue loop is on, and it is off by default: use the `autoplay` option (the default for new queues) or `player.queue.setAutoplay(guildID, enabled?)` (one queue, switches the status when `enabled` is not passed). The tracks that were added are announced with the `autoplayAdded` event `(queue, tracks)`. Without the autoplay nothing changed: the queue ends with `queueEnded` (`ended`).

**`autoAddingTracks` is not the autoplay.** It only tells whether `player.search()` (and a collector) adds the found track to the queue by itself; it does nothing when the queue ends. See the [Providers page](providers.md#autoplay-and-related-tracks) for how the related tracks are found.

### Tracks that can not be played

A track that can not be played is reported with the `error` event and **skipped**, the queue continues with the next track (in 1.x the queue could hang). If the voice connection is lost, the queue is closed.

### New and changed events

```diff
+ player#providerFailed
+ player#sourceUsed
+ player#ytdlpStatus
+ player#skippedTrack
+ player#autoplayAdded
```

**`queueEnded` changed:** it now has a second argument `reason` and is emitted once every time a queue is closed, not only when the tracks are over: `reason` is `ended` (the tracks are over, the only case in 1.x), `stopped` (`queue.stop()`), `deleted` (`queue.delete()`), `skipped` (the last track was skipped) or `error` (the voice connection failed). Handlers of 1.x `(queue) => ...` keep working, but they now also run in the new cases: use `if(reason === 'ended')` to keep the old behaviour.

`sourceUsed` also has `via` (the provider that gave the audio, when a provider plays the audio of another one).

`providerFailed` has `{ provider, method, error }` and is emitted when a source provider fails and the next one is used. `sourceUsed` has `{ provider, track, seek, prefetched }` and tells which provider gives the audio of a track (a debugging event). `ytdlpStatus` has `{ stage, message, origin, path, version, latest, reason }` and reports every step of finding, checking, downloading and updating yt-dlp (`stage` is `found`, `checking`, `up-to-date`, `update-available`, `downloading`, `installed`, `skipped` (see `reason`: `update-disabled`, `interval`, `offline`, `custom-command`) or `error`). `skippedTrack` has `{ track, next, error }` and is emitted when a track could not be played and the queue goes on with the next one. Every `Player` now has its own event emitter (in 1.x all players shared one).

### New and changed options

See the [Providers page](providers.md) for the source providers, the order of the sources and writing your own provider.

```diff
+ options.sources            // source providers, [YoutubeiProvider, YtDlpProvider] by default
+ options.lyrics             // lyrics provider, LrclibProvider by default
+ options.playlistLimit      // tracks taken from a playlist link, 100
+ options.prefetchSeconds    // the next track is prepared in advance, 20
+ options.autoplay, options.autoplayLimit, options.autoplayHistory, options.autoplayMaxDuration // the autoplay, see "Autoplay" below
+ options.sourceFailureThreshold, options.sourceCooldown

+ options.collectorsConfig.message.cancel, options.collectorsConfig.reaction.cancel // the cancel word (`cancel`) and the cancel reaction (`❌`), `false` turns them off
* options.collectorsConfig.*.attempts // every message or reaction of the user is an attempt, the user can try again while there are attempts
* options.synchronLoop       // `false` is not replaced with `true` any more
* invalid options          // an option that is passed but is wrong (for example `time: 60000` instead of `'1m'`) is still replaced with the default value, but the module tells about it with `console.warn`
- options.databaseConfig                // removed together with the server playlists, see "Removed" below
```

### Methods

Names are the same as in 1.1.7. What changed:

```diff
* player.search(query, member, channel)       // a playlist link adds all its tracks and starts playing, returns an array of tracks; throws TRACK_NOT_FOUND
* player.lyrics(query)                        // LRCLIB; returns { query, result, title, artist, source }; throws LYRICS_NOT_FOUND
* player.createCollector(...)                 // rejects with COLLECTOR_TIMEOUT or COLLECTOR_CANCELLED, the reaction collector adds a cancel reaction
* player.queue.setFilter(guildID, filter)     // continues from the current position
* player.queue.removeTrack(guildID, 0)        // removing the playing track skips it
* player.queue.setVolume(guildID)             // without a value sets the default volume
* player.queue.seek(guildID, seconds)         // validates the value
+ player.sources                              // SourceRegistry
+ player.queue.setAutoplay(guildID, enabled?)   // turns the autoplay of a queue on or off, see "Autoplay" below
+ player.utils.parseDuration(text)             // '10m' -> milliseconds
+ player.utils.formatMilliseconds(ms, { long }) // milliseconds -> '2m' or '2 minutes'
+ player.utils.splitMilliseconds(ms)           // milliseconds -> { days, hours, minutes, seconds }
+ player.lyricsProvider
```

New enum value: `Search.PLAYLIST`.

### Types and imports

Types are generated from the code and exported from the main package. The `discord-player-music/types/...` files do not exist any more.

```diff
- import { PlayerTrack } from 'discord-player-music/types/PlayerData';
+ import type { PlayerTrack } from 'discord-player-music';
```

The package has two builds, ESM (`import`) and CommonJS (`require`), both work.

### Removed

* `ytdl-core` and `yt-search` and everything that depended on them. If you used the `Status code: 403/404` errors of `ytdl-core`, check `providerFailed` and `error` events instead.
* `lyrics-finder` (it stopped finding lyrics). Use the `lyrics` option for another service.
* `player.utils.getUniqueID()` (it was only needed by the server playlists; use `crypto.randomUUID()` if you need an ID) and the unused error texts `playingPaused` and `playingResumed` of `player.errors` (an already paused or already playing queue gives the `INVALID_STATE` error). `player.utils.getTrackDuration(url)` is **deprecated**: it still works, but the duration is in the tracks that `player.search()` returns (`track.duration`) and `player.sources.resolve(url)` gives `seconds`.
* **Server playlists** (the playlists of a Discord server saved by the module) and the JSON database that kept them. They were in 1.x and are removed in 2.0 without deprecated aliases, so code that uses them stops working (breaking change): it is an extra feature that every bot can build for itself in a few lines.

```diff
- player.playlists.create / addTrack / play / removeTrack / delete
- player.database.get / write / initGuild
- options.databaseConfig, options.databaseConfig.path, options.databaseConfig.checkInterval
- player#createdPlaylist, player#deletedPlaylist, Events.PLAYLIST_CREATED, Events.PLAYLIST_DELETED
- GuildPlaylist, PlaylistTrack, CreatePlaylistData, AddPlaylistData, DatabaseManagerConfiguration, DatabaseStorage
- PlayerErrorCode.PLAYLIST_NOT_FOUND, GUILD_PLAYLISTS_NOT_FOUND, PLAYLIST_TRACK_NOT_FOUND, PLAYLIST_TRACK_EXISTS
- PlaylistsManager, DatabaseManager
```

  The module does not read or write the `dpm.playlists.json` file any more. You can delete it, or read it yourself (it is plain JSON: `{ "<guildID>": { "playlists": [{ "id", "title", "author", "tracks": [{ "url", "title" }], ... }] } }`) to move your old playlists to your own storage. Playing a **YouTube** playlist link is a different feature and stays (`player.search()` with a playlist link, `playlistLimit`).

  To keep playlists yourself, store the links in any storage (a `Map`, a database, a JSON file) and add them one by one with `player.search()`, it keeps their order:

```ts
const playlists = new Map<string, Array<string>>(); // playlist name -> track links
playlists.set('chill', ['https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Vt2TeOptLxE', 'https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1Qo35ldlvWo']);

// Play the playlist: every link is added to the queue, the first one starts playing
for(const url of playlists.get('chill') ?? []) await player.search(url, message.member, message.channel);
```

changelog.name: Changelog
changelog.content:
# Module Changelog
* ***Version 1.0.0***
  * Release module
* ***Version 1.0.1***
  * Code optimization
  * Fix methods `joinVoiceChannel()` and `leaveVoiceChannel()`
  * Added the `formatNumbers()` method for formatting numbers
  * Fix bugs
  * Fix `README.md`
* ***Version 1.0.2***
  * Code optimization
  * Fixed bug with repeating song/queue
  * Improving the quality of playing songs
  * Added filter system. Method `setFilter()`
  * Changing the returned data by some methods and events
  * Added the `getGuildMap()` method to get the server queue object
* ***Version 1.0.3***
  * Code optimization
  * Fix caught some bugs
  * Fixed minor bugs
  * Rewrite `README.md`
  * Fixed events
* ***Versions 1.0.4 - 1.0.5***
  * Update versions all dependencies
  * Fix `README.md`
* ***Version 1.0.6***
  * Fix module typings
  * Fix minor bugs
  * Added the `getFilters()` method to get arrays with player filters
  * Fix `README.md`
* ***Version 1.0.7***
  * Update versions all dependencies
* ***Version 1.0.8***
  * Fix method `searchVideo()`
  * Added the `getLyrics()` method to get lyrics for current song
* ***Version 1.1.0***
  * Fix filter system
  * Added the `shuffle()` method for shuffling songs in queue
* ***Version 1.1.1***
  * The `playerError` event has started to catch more errors about which users can be warned
  * When receiving an error `Status code: 403`, the module will restart the stream (previously, the stream simply ended)
  * Add the `removeSong()` method for removing songs from the queue
  * Completely rewritten `README.md`
  * Release of module documentation. Link: [dpm-docs](https://dpm-docs.tk)
* ***Version 1.1.2***
  * Updating the documentation for the new design style
  * The module structure has been completely rewritten
  * Added class `Utils`, some methods have been moved to it and marked as `public`
* ***Version 1.1.3***
  * Remove dependency on `<Discord.Message>` completely
  * The `searchVideo()` method has been replaced with `searchSong()`
  * Completely rewritten TypeScript code
  * The `getSongIndex()` and `addSong()` methods have been changed
  * The `playerError` event have been changed
* ***Version 1.1.5***
  * The module structure has been completely rewritten on managers
  * Completely rewritten `README.md`
  * Rewritten TypeScript code
  * Correction of bugs and errors
  * Adding support for `discord.js v13`
  * and many other changes...
* ***Version 1.1.6***
  * Fix Voice Manager
* ***Version 1.1.7***
  * The module has been completely rewritten to the new structure and the TypeScript language
  * Replaced old domain [dpm-docs](https://dpm-docs.tk) with new one [dpm-website](https://dpm.js.org)
  * Added new managers, simplified work with old ones
  * Optimization of module algorithms
  * Added server playlist functionality
  * Removed support for `discord.js v12` and added support for the current `discord.js v14`
  * Updated dependency versions to the latest ones
  * Updated old and added new events
  * Partial transition to enumerated types (enum)
  * The rest of the changes can be seen more clearly on the updates page...

* ***Version 2.0.0***
  * **Breaking:** Node.js 22.12.0 or newer and discord.js 14.28 or newer are required, `@discordjs/voice` was updated to 0.19
  * **Breaking:** methods throw `PlayerError` (with `code`, `status` and `cause`) instead of returning `{ error }`, see the updating page
  * Fixed YouTube playback: `ytdl-core` and `yt-search` were replaced with replaceable source providers (`SourceRegistry`, `YoutubeiProvider`, `YtDlpProvider`)
  * Automatic fallback between providers, the `providerFailed`, `sourceUsed` (which source plays a track), `ytdlpStatus` (every step of finding, checking, downloading and updating yt-dlp) and `skippedTrack` (a track could not be played, the queue goes on with the next one) events and the `sources`, `sourceFailureThreshold` and `sourceCooldown` options
  * `yt-dlp` is found in `PATH` or downloaded automatically when the player starts (the checksum is verified), and a newer release is installed at every start; the `cookies` option (one cookies file for both `youtubei.js` and yt-dlp: `youtubei.js` reads the information of age-restricted videos and private playlists with it, yt-dlp plays them) for servers where YouTube asks to sign in
  * `SIGN_IN_REQUIRED` error for age-restricted videos and bot checks (the cookies are needed)
  * yt-dlp errors are thrown before the stream starts (so the next provider is used) and explain the sign-in request
  * YouTube playlist links: all tracks are added to the queue and start playing (`playlistLimit` option, `Search.PLAYLIST`)
  * The next track is prepared in advance (`prefetchSeconds` option), no pause between tracks
  * Lyrics from LRCLIB (`lyrics-finder` stopped working), the `lyrics` option and `LyricsProvider` interface
  * Tracks that can not be played are skipped, the queue no longer hangs
  * Every `Player` has its own event emitter, an `error` event without listeners no longer crashes the process
  * Collectors: the user can cancel a selection (the word `cancel` or the `❌` reaction, `COLLECTOR_CANCELLED`), wrong answers use up the attempts and the user can try again (a wrong answer ended with a timeout error before), emojis are compared without the invisible variation selector (a reaction could be ignored), the message of the small-number error showed `{max}` instead of the minimum; `createCollector()` is covered by tests
  * Fixed: removing the playing track skipped the next one; `synchronLoop: false` was ignored; `setVolume()` without a value; collectors never finished; leaking listeners on every track; the filter restarted the track from the beginning; `VoiceManager#join` crash
  * `SourceProvider` is extended for external packages: the optional `attach` and `audioProvider` members, the `via` field of the `sourceUsed` event, the error codes `SOURCE_RATE_LIMITED`, `SOURCE_UNAUTHORIZED` and `AUDIO_NOT_FOUND`, and `SourcePlaylist` is exported.
  * Removed (breaking change, no deprecated aliases): server playlists from 1.x (`player.playlists`, the events `createdPlaylist` and `deletedPlaylist`, the related types and error codes) and the JSON database that kept them (`player.database`, `databaseConfig`). It is an extra feature that every bot can build for itself, see the [updating page](updating.md) for a short example. Playing a YouTube playlist link is not removed
  * Removed `player.utils.getUniqueID()` and two unused error texts; `player.utils.getTrackDuration()` is deprecated
  * **Autoplay:** when the tracks are over (and no loop is on) the module finds related tracks, adds them and goes on playing them until it is turned off: the `autoplay`, `autoplayLimit`, `autoplayHistory` and `autoplayMaxDuration` options, `player.queue.setAutoplay()`, the `autoplayAdded` event, `Search.AUTOPLAY`, the optional `related()` method of `SourceProvider` (`YoutubeiProvider` uses the up next feed of YouTube, the other providers fall back to a search by the author and the title). `autoAddingTracks` is not the autoplay: it only adds the result of `player.search()` to the queue
  * `YoutubeiProvider` hides the parser warnings of `youtubei.js` (the `warnings` option shows them)
  * New helpers `player.utils.parseDuration()` (`'10m'` to milliseconds), `player.utils.formatMilliseconds()` (milliseconds to `2m` or `2 minutes`) and `player.utils.splitMilliseconds()` (milliseconds to days, hours, minutes and seconds)
  * **Changed:** `queueEnded` now has a second argument `reason` (`ended`, `stopped`, `deleted`, `skipped`, `error`) and is emitted once every time a queue is closed, not only when the tracks are over (check `reason === 'ended'` for the old behaviour). Invalid options are still replaced with the defaults, but the module now tells about them with `console.warn`
  * Types are generated from the code, ESM and CommonJS builds, JSDoc for the whole public API
  * Added tests, linting, a JSDoc check and CI workflows

props.name: sources
props.description: Player Source Registry. Providers are tried in order of priority.

methods.name: initGuildTrack
methods.description: Allows you to initialize the next track for playback. A track that can not be played is reported with the `error` event and skipped.When no track is passed, the queue is ended.
examples: const searchResults = await client.player.search('Query', message.member, message.channel);client.player.initGuildTrack('GuildID', searchResults[0]);

returns.description: Resolves when the track has started

methods.name: search
methods.description: Allows you to search for tracks by link/title using the source providers. A playlist link adds all its tracks to the queue and starts playing them.
examples: const searchData = await client.player.search('Xtrullor - Samsara', message.member, message.channel);console.log(searchData);

returns.description: Array with search results. For a video link it is one track, for a playlist link it is all the tracks of the playlist (up to `playlistLimit`). Links are added to the queue if `autoAddingTracks` is enabled, a playlist starts playing from its first track.

methods.name: lyrics
methods.description: Allows you to find lyrics for songs by their name (LRCLIB by default, see the `lyrics` option)
examples: const lyricsData = await client.player.lyrics('Imagine Dragons - Thunder');return message.channel.send({ content: `${lyricsData.query}\n\n${lyricsData.result}` });

returns.description: Query, lyrics and the song title and artist (if the provider knows them)

methods.name: initQueueTrack
methods.description: Allows you to add a track from the search results to the queue
examples: const searchData = await client.player.search('Xtrullor - Samsara', message.member, message.channel);await client.player.initQueueTrack(1, searchData);

params.name: index
params.description: Track number in the results (starting from 1)

returns.description: Resolves when the track has been added

methods.name: createCollector
methods.description: Allows you to create a collector to select a track from a list.The message collector waits for a number in the messages of the user, the reaction collector waits for a reaction with a number(the bot needs the *Add Reactions* and *Read Message History* permissions and the `GuildMessageReactions` intent for it).Every message or reaction of the user is an attempt (see `collectorsConfig.*.attempts`); the cancel word (`cancel`) or the cancel reaction (`❌`) cancels the selection.The selected track is added to the queue when `autoAddingTracks` is enabled.
examples: const searchData = await client.player.search('Xtrullor - Samsara', message.member, message.channel);// Reaction collector (up to 10 results)if(searchData.length <= 10) client.player.createCollector(Collector.REACTION, message, searchData, 'UserID');// Message collectorif(searchData.length > 1) {     const msg = await message.channel.send({ content: searchData.map((track, index) => `${index + 1} ${track.title}`).join('\n') });     client.player.createCollector(Collector.MESSAGE, msg, searchData, 'UserID');}

params.name: message
params.description: Discord Guild Message (the message with the list of tracks that the bot sent)

params.name: userID
params.description: Requested user ID (required for the reaction collector)

returns.description: Selected track, its number and the list of tracks

methods.name: init
methods.description: Method for initializing module

methods.name: on
methods.description: Method for listening Player events

methods.name: once
methods.description: Method to listen for an Player event only once

methods.name: emit
methods.description: Method for emits Player events

returns.description: `true` if the event had listeners (an `error` event without listeners is printed to the console)

events.name: ready
events.description: Emits when the module is ready

events.name: error
events.description: Emitted when a module can't do anything and gets an error

events.name: addedTrack
events.description: Emitted when a new track is added to the server queue

events.name: playingTrack
events.description: Emitted when a new track starts playing in the server queue

events.name: queueStarted
events.description: Emitted when a new server queue is started

events.name: queueEnded
events.description: Emitted once every time a server queue is closed and removed, for any reason: the tracks are over, `queue.stop()`, `queue.delete()`, the last track was skippedor the voice connection failed. The second argument tells why. Use `reason === 'ended'` to react only when the queue finishes playing by itself (the only case in 1.x).

params.name: reason
params.description: Why the queue was closed: `ended` (the tracks are over), `stopped` (`queue.stop()`), `deleted` (`queue.delete()`), `skipped` (the last track was skipped) or `error` (the voice connection failed)

events.name: autoplayAdded
events.description: Emitted when the autoplay found related tracks and added them to the end of the queue (the tracks are played right after; `addedTrack` is not emitted for them)

params.name: tracks
params.description: Added tracks (`searchType` is `Search.AUTOPLAY`, `requested` and the channels are the ones of the track that played before)

events.name: queueStateChange
events.description: Emitted when the playback state of the server queue changes.

methods.name: on
methods.description: Method for listening Player events

methods.name: once
methods.description: Method to listen for an Player event only once

methods.name: emit
methods.description: Method for emits Player events

returns.description: `true` if the event had listeners (an `error` event without listeners is printed to the console)

construct.name: PlayerError

params.name: params
params.description: Values for the placeholders of the message

examples: try {    await client.player.queue.skipTrack('GuildID');}catch(error) {    if(error instanceof PlayerError && error.code === PlayerErrorCode.QUEUE_NOT_FOUND) return message.channel.send({ content: 'Nothing is playing!' });    throw error;}

construct.name: LrclibProvider
examples: const player = new Player(client, { lyrics: new LrclibProvider({ timeout: 5000 }) });

methods.name: search
methods.description: Searches lyrics by a query

returns.description: Lyrics or `null` if nothing was found

methods.name: add
methods.description: Allows you to register a new filter (the value is passed to FFmpeg as `-af`)
examples: const addData = await client.player.filters.add('quiet', 'volume=0.5');if(addData.status) console.log('Filter has been registered!');

methods.name: isExists
methods.description: Allows you to check whether a filter is registered
examples: const exists = await client.player.filters.isExists('bassboost');

methods.name: get
methods.description: Allows you to get a filter by name
examples: const filter = await client.player.filters.get('bassboost');console.log(filter.value);

methods.name: list
methods.description: Allows you to get all registered filters
examples: const filters = await client.player.filters.list();console.log([...filters.keys()].join(', '));

methods.name: delete
methods.description: Allows you to delete a filter
examples: const deleteData = await client.player.filters.delete('quiet');

methods.name: find
methods.description: Returns the queue of the server or throws an error

methods.name: add
methods.description: Allows you to add a track to the server queue. If the server has no queue, a new one is created and playback starts.
examples:
const searchData = await client.player.search('Xtrullor - Samsara', message.member, message.channel);
const isAdded = await client.player.queue.add(searchData[0]);

methods.name: startTrack
methods.description:
Starts playing a track of the queue. When the track is not passed, the queue has ended and is deleted.
A track that can not be played is reported with the `error` event and skipped.

returns.description: Resolves when the track has started (or the queue has ended)

methods.name: playTrack
methods.description: Creates an audio stream of the track and plays it (the current playback is replaced)

params.name: seek
params.description: Position to start from, in seconds

returns.description: Resolves when the playback has started

methods.name: nextTrack
methods.description: Track that is played after the current one

returns.description: Next track (the same track when the track loop is enabled)

methods.name: schedulePrefetch
methods.description: Plans the preparation of the next track: it starts a few seconds before the current track ends (see the `prefetchSeconds` option)

params.name: position
params.description: Position the track started from, in seconds

methods.name: startPrefetch
methods.description: Creates the stream of the next track in advance (errors are ignored here: the track is simply created again when its turn comes)

methods.name: cancelPrefetch
methods.description: Cancels the preparation of the next track and closes the stream that was prepared

methods.name: refreshPrefetch
methods.description: The queue was changed (tracks removed or shuffled, loop mode switched): the prepared stream may be the wrong one, so it is prepared again

methods.name: handleIdle
methods.description: Called when the audio player became idle: the current track has ended (or was skipped), so the next one is played

returns.description: Resolves when the next track has started

methods.name: handlePlayerError
methods.description: Called when the audio player got an error while playing (for example the stream was interrupted)

methods.name: setState
methods.description: Allows you to change the playback state of the server queue (pause or resume)
examples:
const stateData = await client.player.queue.setState('GuildID', GuildQueueState.PAUSED);
if(stateData.status) return message.channel.send({ content: 'Playback has been paused!' });

params.name: type
params.description: New state. If it is not passed, the paused queue is resumed.

methods.name: get
methods.description: Allows you to get the queue of the server
examples:
const guildQueue = await client.player.queue.get('GuildID');

console.log(guildQueue.tracks);

methods.name: progress
methods.description: Allows you to get the progress bar of the current track

methods.name: streamInfo
methods.description: Allows you to get information about the queue playback
examples:
const streamData = await client.player.queue.streamInfo('GuildID');

console.log(streamData);

returns.description: Loop, filter, state, volume and the time since the queue started

methods.name: trackInfo
methods.description: Allows you to get a track of the queue
examples:
const trackData = await client.player.queue.trackInfo('GuildID', 1);

console.log(trackData.title);

params.name: index
params.description: Track index (the current track by default)

returns.description: Track (the current one if there is no track with that index)

methods.name: setFilter
methods.description: Allows you to set a filter for the queue playback. The current track continues from the current position.
examples:
const filterData = await client.player.queue.setFilter('GuildID', 'bassboost');

console.log(filterData.name);

methods.name: setLoop
methods.description: Allows you to switch the loop mode of the queue
examples:
const loopData = await client.player.queue.setLoop('GuildID', Loop.QUEUE);

console.log(loopData);

params.name: type
params.description: Loop type (the current track by default)

returns.description: Loop status of the track and the queue

methods.name: setVolume
methods.description: Allows you to set the playback volume of the queue
examples:
const volumeData = await client.player.queue.setVolume('GuildID', 10);
if(volumeData.status) return message.channel.send({ content: 'Volume has been changed!' });

params.name: value
params.description: Volume (the default volume if it is not passed)

methods.name: skipTrack
methods.description: Allows you to skip the current track
examples:
const skipData = await client.player.queue.skipTrack('GuildID');

console.log(`${skipData.current.title} -> ${skipData.next?.title}`);

returns.description: Skipped and next track (`null` if the queue has ended)

methods.name: removeTrack
methods.description: Allows you to remove a track from the queue. Removing the current track (index 0) skips it.
examples:
const removeData = await client.player.queue.removeTrack('GuildID', 2);

console.log(removeData.deleted.title);

returns.description: Removed track and the updated track list

methods.name: seek
methods.description: Allows you to rewind the current track to the given position

methods.name: shuffle
methods.description: Allows you to shuffle the tracks of the queue (the current track stays in place)
examples:
const shuffleData = await client.player.queue.shuffle('GuildID');

console.log(shuffleData.map(track => track.title));

methods.name: stop
methods.description: Allows you to stop the playback: the bot leaves the voice channel and the queue is deleted
examples:
const stopData = await client.player.queue.stop('GuildID');
if(stopData.status) return message.channel.send({ content: 'Playback has been stopped!' });

methods.name: delete
methods.description: Allows you to delete the queue of the server without leaving the voice channel
examples: const deleteData = await client.player.queue.delete('GuildID');

methods.name: setAutoplay
methods.description:
Allows you to turn the autoplay of the server queue on or off. With the autoplay, when the tracks are over (and no loop is on, and after the last
track is skipped or removed), the module finds tracks related to the track that played last, adds them to the queue and plays them, again and again,
until the autoplay is turned off or the queue is stopped. Without it the queue ends (`queueEnded` with the reason `ended`).
examples:
const autoplayData = await client.player.queue.setAutoplay('GuildID', true);

console.log(autoplayData.autoplay);

params.name: enabled
params.description: New status (the status is switched when it is not passed)

methods.name: isAutoplaying
methods.description: Checks that the autoplay may add tracks now: it is on and neither the track loop nor the queue loop is on

returns.description: `true` if the autoplay works for the queue

methods.name: remember
methods.description: Remembers a played (or failed) track, so the autoplay does not add it again. The oldest tracks are forgotten (see `autoplayHistory`).

methods.name: autoplay
methods.description:
Autoplay: when the queue has no more tracks, it looks for tracks related to the track that played last, adds them and goes on playing.
Nothing is added (and the queue ends) when the autoplay is off, a loop is on, nothing suitable was found or the lookup failed (`error` event).
Live streams, tracks longer than `autoplayMaxDuration` and the tracks that already played are skipped.

returns.description: `true` if the queue must not be closed (the playback went on, or the queue was closed meanwhile)

methods.name: toSourceTrack
methods.description: Converts a track of the queue to the track of a source provider (the providers use its `url`)

methods.name: createAutoplayTrack
methods.description: Creates a track of the queue from a related track: the requester and the channels are the ones of the track that played before

methods.name: formatnumbers
methods.description: Allows you to format numbers to the `00` form
examples: const formatData = client.player.utils.formatnumbers([1, 2, 3, 10]);// Result: ['01', '02', '03', '10']console.log(formatData);

methods.name: formatDuration
methods.description: Allows you to format a duration in seconds to the `00:00:00` form
examples: const duration = client.player.utils.formatDuration(307);// Result: 00:05:07console.log(duration);

methods.name: parseDuration
methods.description: Allows you to read a duration written as text and get milliseconds. A number without a unit is milliseconds.
examples: const milliseconds = client.player.utils.parseDuration('10m');// Result: 600000console.log(milliseconds);

params.name: value
params.description: Duration: a number with an optional unit, for example `500`, `10s`, `1.5 hours`, `2d`, `1 week`

methods.name: splitMilliseconds
methods.description: Allows you to split milliseconds into days, hours, minutes and seconds (every part is a whole number, the hours, minutes and seconds arethe remainders: `90061000` is 1 day, 1 hour, 1 minute and 1 second)
examples: const time = client.player.utils.splitMilliseconds(90061000);// Result: { days: 1, hours: 1, minutes: 1, seconds: 1 }console.log(time);

methods.name: formatMilliseconds
methods.description: Allows you to write milliseconds as a short or a long text
examples: const text = client.player.utils.formatMilliseconds(120000, { long: true });// Result: 2 minutesconsole.log(text);

methods.name: parseUnits
methods.description: Reads a number with a unit (`10s`, `1.5 hours`)

returns.description: Milliseconds, or `undefined` if the text is not a duration

methods.name: formatShort
methods.description: Short text: `2m`

methods.name: formatLong
methods.description: Long text: `2 minutes`

methods.name: plural
methods.description: Writes a number of units with the unit name (the plural form is used from one and a half units)

methods.name: checkOptions
methods.description: Allows you to check the module options and fill the missing or invalid values with the defaults
examples: const playerOptions = client.player.utils.checkOptions();console.log(playerOptions);

methods.name: pick
methods.description: Returns the value if it has the expected type, otherwise the default value (and tells about it when the option was passed)

params.name: name
params.description: Option name for the warning (nothing is reported when it is not passed)

methods.name: warnOption
methods.description: Tells in the console that an option is invalid and its default value is used

methods.name: isDuration
methods.description: Checks that a text is a valid duration (see `parseDuration`)

returns.description: `true` if the text can be read as a duration

methods.name: validated
methods.description: Returns the option when it is valid, otherwise `undefined` (and tells about it when the option was passed)

methods.name: createEmptyProgress
methods.description: Allows you to create an empty track progress bar
examples: const emptyProgress = client.player.utils.createEmptyProgress();// Result: 🔘▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬console.log(emptyProgress);

methods.name: getTrackDuration
methods.description: Allows you to find out the duration of the track
examples: const trackDuration = await client.player.utils.getTrackDuration('https://youtube.com/watch?v=Vt2TeOptLxE');// Result: 307console.log(trackDuration);
methods.deprecated: It stays for the code of 1.x and will be removed. The duration is in the tracks that `player.search()` returns (`track.duration`), and `player.sources.resolve(url)` gives `seconds`.

returns.description: Track duration in seconds (0 if it can not be received)

methods.name: join
methods.description: Allows the bot to join a voice channel on the server
examples: const channel = message.guild?.channels.cache.get('ChannelID');if(channel && channel.isVoiceBased()) await client.player.voice.join(channel);

methods.name: leave
methods.description: Allows the bot to leave the server's voice channel
examples: const guildConnection = await client.player.voice.leave('GuildID');return message.channel.send({ content: `Client leave from ${message.guild.channels.cache.get(guildConnection.joinConfig.channelId)} channel!` });

construct.name: SourceRegistry

props.name: list

params.name: index

methods.name: unregister
methods.description: Removes a provider

methods.name: attempt
methods.description: Runs an action on providers one by one until one succeeds

params.name: method
params.description: Method name (used for events and errors)

returns.description: Result of the first successful provider

methods.name: forURL
methods.description: Providers that can handle the URL, in order of priority

methods.description: Searches tracks by text query

methods.description: Gets track information by URL

methods.description: Checks whether the URL is a playlist link that one of the providers can load

methods.name: resolvePlaylist
methods.description: Gets the tracks of a playlist by URL

methods.name: related
methods.description: Finds tracks related to a track (for the autoplay). The providers that can find related tracks (`related`) are tried in order, with the samefailure counter as the other operations. When none of them gives tracks, the tracks are searched by the author and the title of the given track.

params.name: track

params.name: options

construct.name: YoutubeiProvider

methods.name: signedClient
methods.description: Returns a signed-in session (made with the cookies), or `null` when there are no cookies.It is used for what a signed-in session can do: information about age-restricted videos and private playlists.

methods.name: parseID

methods.description: Creates the InnerTube session ahead of time, so the first search does not wait for it. The player calls it when it is created.

The player calls it when it is created, so the first track does not wait for the download.The update check (when yt-dlp is managed by the module) compares the installed version with the latest release and downloads the new one.

props.name: autoAddingTracks
props.description: Whether `player.search()` (and a collector) adds the found track to the queue by itself. It is **not** the autoplay: it does nothing when the queue ends, see `autoplay`

props.name: autoplay
props.description: The autoplay of new queues: when the tracks are over and no loop is on, related tracks are found, added to the queue and played, again and again (`queue.setAutoplay()` switches it for a server)

props.name: autoplayLimit
props.description: How many related tracks the autoplay adds at once (a few tracks let the next track be prepared in advance)

props.name: autoplayHistory
props.description: How many played tracks are remembered, so the autoplay does not add them again

props.name: autoplayMaxDuration
props.description: The autoplay skips tracks that are longer (and live streams)

props.name: searchResultsLimit
props.description: number of results to be returned when searching for tracks by title

props.name: playlistLimit
props.description: Maximum number of tracks that are taken from a playlist link

props.name: sourceFailureThreshold
props.description: After this many failures in a row a source provider is used last for a while (the next tracks go to the next provider first)

props.name: sourceCooldown
props.description: For how long a failing source provider is used last

props.name: cookies
props.description: Path of a cookies file (Netscape format) with the cookies of a signed-in YouTube account. It is used by both default providers (`youtubei.js` and `yt-dlp`). Needed when YouTube asks the server to sign in, see the FAQ.

props.name: prefetchSeconds
props.description: The audio of the next track is prepared this many seconds before the current track ends, so there is no pause between tracks (0 disables it)

props.name: sources
props.description: Track source providers in order of priority (YoutubeiProvider and YtDlpProvider by default)

props.name: collectorsConfig.message.attempts
props.description: Maximum number of attempts to select a track (every message of the user is an attempt)

props.name: collectorsConfig.message.cancel
props.description: The word that cancels the selection (`false` turns the cancel word off)

props.name: collectorsConfig.reaction.attempts
props.description: Maximum number of attempts to select a track (every reaction of the user is an attempt)

props.name: collectorsConfig.reaction.cancel
props.description: The reaction that cancels the selection, it is added after the numbers (`false` turns it off)

props.name: provider
props.description: Name of the provider that failed

props.name: QUEUE_ENDED
props.description: Player 'queueEnded' event (a queue was closed for any reason, the second argument tells why)

props.name: AUTOPLAY_ADDED
props.description: Player 'autoplayAdded' event (the autoplay added related tracks to the queue)

props.name: PROVIDER_FAILED
props.description: Player 'providerFailed' event (a source provider failed, the next one is tried)

props.name: YTDLP_STATUS
props.description: Player 'ytdlpStatus' event (a step of finding, checking, downloading or updating yt-dlp)

props.name: SOURCE_USED
props.description: Player 'sourceUsed' event (which source provider gives the audio of a track)

props.name: TRACK_SKIPPED
props.description: Player 'skippedTrack' event (a track could not be played and the queue goes on with the next one)

props.name: PAUSED
props.description: Playback is paused (waiting to be restored)

props.name: PLAYING
props.description: Playback is active and not stopped

props.name: PLAYLIST
props.description: Search playlist link value (all tracks of the playlist are returned)

props.name: AUTOPLAY
props.description: The track was added by the autoplay (it is related to the track that played before)

typedefs.name: PlayerErrorCode
typedefs.description: Codes of the errors thrown by the module

props.name: MISSING_PARAMETER
props.description: A required parameter was not passed

props.name: INVALID_TYPE
props.description: A parameter has an invalid data type

props.name: INVALID_VALUE
props.description: A parameter has an invalid value

props.name: QUEUE_TRACK_NOT_FOUND
props.description: There is no track with the given index in the queue

props.name: SHUFFLE_UNAVAILABLE
props.description: There are not enough tracks in the queue to shuffle

props.name: INVALID_STATE
props.description: The queue can not be switched to the given playback state

props.name: USER_NOT_IN_VOICE
props.description: The user is not in a voice channel

props.name: ALREADY_CONNECTED
props.description: The client is already connected to a voice channel

props.name: CONNECTION_FAILED
props.description: The client can not connect to the voice channel

props.name: GUILD_NOT_FOUND
props.description: The server does not exist on the client

props.name: TRACK_NOT_FOUND
props.description: No track was found by the title or link

props.name: SIGN_IN_REQUIRED
props.description: YouTube asks to sign in (age-restricted video or a bot check): the cookies of an account are needed

props.name: COLLECTOR_NO_RESULTS
props.description: The collector got an empty list of results

props.name: COLLECTOR_UNKNOWN
props.description: The collector can not handle that many results

props.name: COLLECTOR_SMALL_VALUE
props.description: The user selected a number that is too small

props.name: COLLECTOR_LARGE_VALUE
props.description: The user selected a number that is too large

props.name: COLLECTOR_TIMEOUT
props.description: The user did not select a track in time

props.name: COLLECTOR_CANCELLED
props.description: The user cancelled the selection (or the list message was deleted)

props.name: SOURCE_RATE_LIMITED
props.description: A service limits the requests, `Retry-After` tells when to try again

props.name: SOURCE_UNAUTHORIZED
props.description: A service did not accept the credentials of the provider

props.name: AUDIO_NOT_FOUND
props.description: A provider that only knows the information of a track did not find its audio in the other sources

props.name: baseURL
props.description: LRCLIB server (you can use your own instance)

props.name: userAgent
props.description: User agent for requests (LRCLIB asks clients to introduce themselves)

typedefs.name: ProviderFailedCallback
typedefs.description: Callback that is called when a provider fails and the registry moves on to the next one

props.name: failureThreshold
props.description: After this many failures in a row (for any tracks) a provider is moved to the end of the list of providers for the given operation

props.name: cooldown
props.description: For how long (in milliseconds) such a provider stays at the end before it is tried first again

props.name: warnings
props.description: Show the parser warnings of `youtubei.js` in the console. YouTube changes its pages often and the library reports what it does not know yet (a page of a video has many such reports), they are not errors. `false` shows only the errors of the library (the log level of `youtubei.js` is global).

props.name: cookies
props.description: Path of a cookies file (Netscape format) with the cookies of a signed-in YouTube account. With it the provider can read information about age-restricted videos and load private playlists (the audio of such videos is played by the next provider, yt-dlp). The same file can be used by `YtDlpProvider`, see the FAQ about the cookies.
